(2) An amendment may be made to the representation of the trade mark if the amendment does not substantially affect the identity of the trade mark as at the time when the particulars of the application were published."}],"answer":"Yes, as an examination step, with a qualification about timing.

• Manual practice: the examiner may request additional information during examination to clearly define the mark’s scope. For a movement mark, the material may include a video clip or sufficient still representations demonstrating the full range of the claimed movement. [TMM/Part10/3/3/6/3]

• Manual practice on outside information: information questioning acceptance can prompt the delegate to begin the revocation process, but another party’s request for revocation alone should not prompt proceedings. The passage does not require immediate revocation whenever outside information raises doubts. [TMM/Part38/2/2/1]

• Act requirement: if clarification involves amending the representation after publication under section 30, section 65(2) permits that amendment only if it does not substantially affect the mark’s identity as at publication. This is legislation, not merely Manual practice. [TMA1995/s65]

The timing qualification is important: the supplied Manual expressly supports requesting clarification ‘At the time of examination’, but does not expressly address a fresh clarification request after acceptance and before revocation begins. I therefore cannot confirm that specific post-acceptance sequence from these passages alone. [TMM/Part10/3/3/6/3; TMM/Part38/2/2/1]"}
